## In plain English
The dogfood failure matches the old #5010 in-harness-ask path: preflight/coach said ask; the operator said yes in chat; the agent tried to stamp from the agent shell and was refused. On tip #7031 already replaced that path for observable-scope and intent-constraint with declared records any shell can write; merge is consent, not the stamp. Prefer-A keeps that tip relief, scrubs rediscovery coach that still points at in-harness-ask for those verbs, and leaves harness-attended completion for remaining human-presence mints as a separate leftover rather than inventing a forgeable chat-yes stamp. #6945 stays the unforgeable approval keep-out.

Reviewed the issue body and all four comments through 7133350292, using pin-read at 60e8921207e77d526c9392a6da1e83345d77a6de. No later comments read. Source and test assertions were inspected, not executed: session:start --read-only failed because the checkout runtime pin is absent.

## C1 — blocks-the-design: deferring P2 does not deliver harness completion

Evidence: draft 7133326261 labels P2 both relieved and operator-deferred, but supplies neither a different issue nor a completion mechanism. The pinned content/contracts/human-origin-authz.md operator-mint inventory retains the human-presence requirement for approved-scope and authz; packages/runtime/src/mint-audit.test.ts explicitly covers the retained approved-scope refusal. Thus the proposed scrub cannot change the remaining leave-harness terminal step.

Failure: binding this draft would report relief while the stated P2 experience stays unchanged. Disposition: remove the relief claim. Either leave P2 explicitly unrelieved, or obtain an actual different-issue deferral through the existing arc process. A placeholder named "leftover" is not that disposition. Do not silently expand this issue into a new authority channel.

## C2 — sharpens-framing: tip cleanup and old-pin recovery are different remedies

Evidence: packages/runtime/src/scope-record-observable-scope.ts already rejects both legacy flags and prints the any-shell declaration usage; packages/core/src/observable-scope/types.ts already coaches that path. The analogous intent writer also rejects the flags. The pinned observable-scope and intent-constraint docs explicitly require upgrading an older reader before writing declared records. The inspected legacy in-harness-ask occurrences include backwards-compatible parser fixtures and another ceiling's stamp, not a demonstrated obsolete coach for these verbs.

Failure: deleting tip strings cannot repair a consumer still running the older runtime; indiscriminate deletion could remove intentional legacy-read coverage. Disposition: make any source scrub conditional on naming an actual reachable stale coach. For old consumers, use the supported runtime-pin upgrade first, then the existing declaration command without --minted-via, landing the record on the delivery merge base before the product change. If no current coach defect is found, prefer a documented existing-path resolution over a speculative new gate or scrub implementation.

## C3 — sharpens-framing: preserve the already-shipped signed branch, not merely a future keep-out

Evidence: packages/core/src/scope-provenance/record-stamp.ts resolves the signed level and verifies approvals through admitSignedRecord. The observable writer already imports decideSignedWrite and exposes --request / --assertion. content/contracts/human-origin-authz.md describes the enrolled-key path with .deft/approvers.json on the merge base.

Failure: unqualified "any shell writes the record; merge is consent" coaching can direct signed-level consumers down a declaration-only route that cannot satisfy their check. It also overstates human consent where bot merge is permitted. Disposition: distinguish unsigned declarations from signed approvals in the remedy. Preserve #6945's existing verification path and #7031's declaration semantics; no chat-yes stamp, trust-file removal, or approval downgrade.

## C4 — footnote: competing remedies and authority boundary

My preferred thin remedy is existing-path recovery: identify the consumer pin and approval level, route to the existing declaration or signed path, and change only a proven stale coach. Keep P2 visibly residual until a real disposition exists. This needs no new approval mechanism.

The strongest competing remedy is a host-owned attended approval channel for approved-scope/authz. It directly addresses P2 and avoids terminal switching. But an agent opening a terminal, replaying chat "yes", supplying --actor, or clearing environment markers does not independently establish a human act. Concurrent worktrees also make an unbound approval vulnerable to application to the wrong request. I would favor that route only with a concrete host capability that authenticates the human event outside agent control and binds admission to the intended authority request and checkout, with replay handling. That is a separately scoped authority design, not a coach-string fix. Preserve the existing human-presence and signed-verification boundaries meanwhile.

The evidence does not require reopening #6945 or inventing another observable/intent stamp. Existing parser compatibility, cohort writers, UAT refusal, merge-base admission and signed verification should remain intact.

## In plain English

The dogfood report describes the old #5010 coach: preflight said ask; the operator said yes in chat; the agent tried `scope:record-observable-scope … --minted-via in-harness-ask` under GROK_* markers and was refused. On tip SHA `60e8921207e77d526c9392a6da1e83345d77a6de` that argv is already dead for observable-scope and intent-constraint: those verbs write `kind: "declared"` from any shell, refuse `--kind` / `--minted-via`, and treat merge as the control. Prefer-A draft 7133326261 tip-binds that relief and correctly keep-outs a forgeable chat-yes stamp and #6945 WebAuthn. The remaining real gap is harness-attended completion for verbs that still keep human-presence mint (`scope:record-approved-scope`, `authz:*`), which belongs as leftover, not a chat stamp for the dropped pair.

## Re-verify (pin-read / dest files at dispatch)

- `packages/runtime/src/scope-record-observable-scope.ts`: WRITER_VERB + REFUSED_FLAGS `--kind`/`--minted-via`; usage states any-shell declared write; `--confirm` accepted and ignored.
- `packages/runtime/src/mint-audit.test.ts`: agent-shell (CLAUDECODE/CI, no TTY) exit 0 writes `kind: "declared"`; `--minted-via=in-harness-ask` exit 2; `isHumanApprovalStamp(declared)` false; approved-scope still refuses without terminal mint.
- `content/contracts/human-origin-authz.md` § Operator mint inventory (#7031): obs/intent rows `dropped; writes kind: "declared"`; approved-scope/authz rows `kept`.
- `packages/core/src/content-contracts/standards/declared_records_7031.test.ts`: worker surfaces must say write-the-declaration and must not coach park / real-TTY land for those verbs.
- Residual rediscovery risk: CHANGELOG still carries the #5010 “in-harness ask … mintedVia: in-harness-ask” narrative; `content/docs/durable-effect-acquisition.md` still shows an `in-harness-ask` example stamp. Tip writer/docs for obs/intent already teach declared any-shell.

## Competing remedies

### Approach A — Tip-bind #7031 + scrub rediscovery + leftover P2 (Prefer-A draft shape; recommended)

Short limbs: (1) bind tip declared any-shell writers for obs/intent; refuse restoring `--minted-via` / in-harness-ask as primary for those verbs; scrub residual #5010 coach that still names ask-then-TTY / `--minted-via in-harness-ask` for them; (2) `operator-deferred: P2 #<new-or-named leftover>` for harness-attended human-presence mint on approved-scope/authz only; (3) keep-out #6945 unforgeable obs/intent approval and refuse a forgeable chat-yes `humanApproval` for those records.

Thin Fail-Closed fit: mechanism is already on tip; this Bound is scrub + defer + keep-out.

### Approach B — Close as already-shipped / duplicate of #7031

Dispose the issue as tip-relieved by #7031 with no Bound product limbs beyond a one-line tip-bind cite. Still requires an explicit leftover (or accepted residual) for the Expected harness-yes path on kept-mint verbs, or that Expected stays unrelieved pain.

Failure mode vs A: under-scrubs rediscovery surfaces (CHANGELOG #5010 prose, durable-effect example, older consumer pins) so the same dogfood argv can recur even when tip writers are correct.

### Approach C — Build harness-yes as primary for obs/intent again

Restore or invent an attended chat-yes that lands obs/intent records (or re-enable `--minted-via in-harness-ask` from the shell that heard yes).

Rejected: forges or weakens declaration-vs-consent (#7031); collides with #6945’s unforgeable keep-out; contradicts tip refuse of `--minted-via` on those writers. Envelope already forbids inventing a forgeable chat-yes stamp for those records.

### Approach D — Absorb #6945 WebAuthn into this Bound

Ship signed zero-terminal approval here so harness-yes becomes cryptographically unforgeable for obs/intent.

Rejected for this issue: #6945 already owns that surface; absorbing it widens blast radius past the dogfood failure (stale coach + refused agent stamp). Keep as keep-out, not co-equal limb.

## Findings

### sharpens-framing — Bound must use closed leftover cite form for P2

Evidence: Prefer-A draft limb `relieves: P2 — operator-deferred: P2 leftover (harness-attended…)` names no different-issue id. Contract/ingest consumers require `operator-deferred: Pn #<issue>` (or true `relieves:`) for pain clearance; prose “leftover” alone leaves unrelieved-pain risk (memory of #5727-class cite form).

Failure mode: successor Bound ships, chip refuses unrelieved P2, Recut thrash on cite form.

Disposition: when parent binds Prefer-A, either file/name the leftover issue and write `operator-deferred: P2 #<id>`, or retract P2 relief and leave P2 residual until that file lands. Do not invent a forgeable harness stamp inside this Bound to “relieve” P2.

### sharpens-framing — Scrub inventory should name residual rediscovery surfaces

Evidence: tip worker surfaces already pass `declared_records_7031` “write the declaration / no park-for-mint” checks, yet CHANGELOG #5010 entry and durable-effect’s `mintedVia: "in-harness-ask"` example still teach the dead path that produced the dogfood argv.

Failure mode: agents or operators reading historical CHANGELOG / adjacent docs rediscover ask → `--minted-via in-harness-ask` and re-hit agent-shell refuse (or try marker unset).

Disposition: Prefer-A Bound scrub limb should name concrete scrub targets (at least CHANGELOG #5010 narrative for obs/intent, durable-effect example if it implies obs/intent mint UX) or accept footnote that historical CHANGELOG stays and only live remediation/commands/skills are SoT — with an explicit parent take either way.

### footnote — Tip already refuses the issue-body argv

`--minted-via=in-harness-ask` on obs/intent is exit 2 on tip (`mint-audit.test.ts`, parseArgs REFUSED_FLAGS). The Exact Expected “yes lands the record” for those verbs is already the declared writer + merge control, not a restored in-harness stamp.

### footnote — Injection / swarm lens

Target changes authority stamps and shell/env markers. Approach C (chat-yes or marker unset) is an injection/self-approval path; Approach A keeps marker refuse and declared≠humanApproval. No extra limb beyond the stated Reject list in draft 7133326261.

## Road not taken

Chose Approach A over B because rediscovery is the live P1 remainder after tip writers shipped; a pure close-as-#7031 under-names scrub. Chose A over C/D per Thin Fail-Closed and the envelope keep-outs (#6945 / no forgeable chat-yes).

## Steelman of rejected Approach C

Strongest case: the operator already answered in the attended harness; forcing a second TTY is pure ceremony once presence was shown. Flip condition: an unforgeable harness attestation that cannot be agent-written (exactly #6945), applied only where consent is still required. For obs/intent on tip, consent already moved to merge under #7031, so C does not relieve the dogfood without reopening declaration-vs-consent.

## Verdict on Prefer-A draft 7133326261

Can bind after the two sharpens above are folded (closed P2 leftover cite; named scrub inventory or explicit historical-CHANGELOG take). Reject list is sound. Do not widen into #6945 or restore in-harness-ask for obs/intent.

metadata.issueBody:
## What happened

Six UI briefs were activated with `plan["x-directive/observableChange"]`. Preflight said ask the human, and on yes the human lands the record. The operator answered in the chat: "please mint for me." The agent ran:

```
scope:record-observable-scope --actor John --confirm --minted-via in-harness-ask -- <brief>
```

## Deny

```
scope:record-observable-scope: refusing operator-cli stamp from an agent/host/CI shell (matched agent-shell env markers: GROK_AGENT, GROK_SESSION_ID). Unset GROK_AGENT, GROK_SESSION_ID and retry from a human interactive TTY
```

Unsetting those markers to get past the check would forge the mint. The operator still has to leave the harness and type `mint` in another terminal. The six briefs are deftai/evolution#2189 through #2194. The operator did then mint them from a TTY. The records are in evolution#2195.

## Expected

A yes from the operator in the attended harness is enough to land the record, or the harness opens the real TTY prompt in the session the operator is already in. An agent-written JSON file must still not count.

## Not the same as

#6945 asks for an approval an agent cannot forge, with no terminal step. This is the current `in-harness-ask` path, which tells the agent to ask and then refuses the only process that heard the answer. #7256 is bulk mint targeting one checkout.
